analysis.errorMessage: Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded. Locator.waitFor: getByRole('button', { name: 'Open Search' }) not visible after 120s
analysis.rootCauseAnalysis: Playwright getByRole() uses accessibility tree. SAP Fiori shell bar search button has HTML title attribute but NO accessible name. Role-based selector cannot find it.
analysis.impact: Blocks all test cases using PurchaseOrderPage.openSearch(). Affects entire CS-2 and CS-3 test suites.

step3_decisionAndAction.decision: CLASSIFICATION: AUTOMATION_BUG (locator strategy issue, not SAP behavior issue)
step3_decisionAndAction.rationale: Phase 5 MCP re-execution conclusively proved that [title="Open Search"] matches the shell bar search button, while getByRole() does not. This is a script locator problem, not an SAP defect.
step3_decisionAndAction.actionDecision: PATCH_SCRIPTS (no escalation to defect logging needed)

patchApplied.rationale: SAP Fiori shell bar uses HTML title attribute for search button, not accessible name. CSS selector is more reliable.

infrastructureIssue.description: Playwright getByRole() cannot locate SAP Fiori shell bar search button because it uses HTML title attribute instead of aria-label or accessible name.
infrastructureIssue.resolution: Use CSS selector [title="Open Search"] to directly target the HTML title attribute.
infrastructureIssue.applicability: ALL test cases using PurchaseOrderPage.openSearch() method

phaseDesignMismatch.finding: Phase 3 comment stated 'Phase 3a MCP confirmed button uses role=button name=Open Search', but Phase 5 re-execution proves this is FALSE.
phaseDesignMismatch.likelyReason: Phase 3 used manual HTML inspection rather than actual Playwright locator testing in a live browser.
phaseDesignMismatch.implication: Phase 3 findings should be validated by Phase 5 re-execution before trusting them.
